answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring staked identity bonds: every agent ID must lock a deposit, the network continuously computes a trust score from verified on-chain interactions, and any ID clustered with fakes is slashed, with its stake burned. Spawning N fake identities therefore costs N bonds plus the near-certain burn of all of them, so the attacker's fable of a thriving agent network collapses like a willow in a storm—no matter how sonnet-smooth its forged reviews sound.
